title: Razavi-Bench: Tracking AI Progress in Analog Circuit Reasoning
abstract: arXiv:2611.20935v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: We propose Razavi-Bench, a benchmark built from the 50 questions in Razavi's two Analog Design Experiments With AI articles and graded by GPT-6 Luna against reference answers and rubrics, and use it to track how fast AI models improve at analog circuit analysis. Across 73 multimodal large language models released between May 2024 and November 2026, the top score rose from 28.83% to 98.33% in 30 months, mostly before the reference answers were published. The leading models now answer almost every textbook question correctly; the hardest questions show a circuit that resembles a textbook one but works differently, or ask about behavior the obvious analysis misses. Within two and a half years, a set of questions that exposed the limits of AI models has become one they answer almost perfectly.

translated_title: Razavi-Bench：追踪AI在模拟电路推理方面的进展
translated_abstract: 我们提出了Razavi-Bench，这是一个基于Razavi的两篇"用AI进行模拟设计实验”文章中的50道题目构建的基准测试，由GPT-6 Luna根据参考答案和评分标准进行评分，并用它来追踪AI模型在模拟电路分析方面进步的速度。在2024年5月至2026年11月间发布的73个多模态大语言模型中，最高分在30个月内从28.83%提升到了98.33%，其中大部分提升发生在参考答案发布之前。领先模型如今几乎能正确回答所有教科书式的问题；而最难的问题展示的是一种看似教科书电路但实际工作方式不同的电路，或者询问显而易见的分析所忽略的行为。在短短两年半内，一组曾暴露出AI模型局限性极限的问题，如今已被它们几乎完美地解答。
tldr: 本文提出了基于Razavi的AI模拟设计实验文章中50道题目构建的Razavi-Bench基准，追踪结果显示AI模型在模拟电路推理能力上于30个月内从28.83%飙升至98.33%，从暴露局限到几乎完美解答。
en_tdlr: We propose Razavi-Bench, a 50-question analog circuit reasoning benchmark, which reveals that top AI models improved from 28.83% to 98.33% accuracy in just 30 months, turning questions that once exposed AI limitations into ones they answer almost perfectly.
